title: Explicit sheafified augmented ring-family complex
statement: Let $(C,J,O)$ be a small ringed site and let $K(A,L)$, $\epsilon(A,L)$ and $m$ be a specified strictly functorial augmented ring-complex family [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. For a finite list $f$ of global sections of $O$, put $L_X=(f_i(X))\subset O(X)$. Define the presheaf complex $P_f(X)=K(O(X),L_X)$, with restrictions $m$, differential inherited from $K$, and augmentation inherited from $\epsilon$. Define its sheaf model by degreewise module sheafification and adjoint transpose of the augmentation. These are actual constructions, parameterized by the given maps, with no data chosen from an existence assertion. Extension of $L_X$ along restriction equals $L_Y$, and the augmentation annihilates boundaries. Complexes and the ring complex use [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech].

proof.text: Ideal.map_span and the section naturality equations identify the restriction ideals. The strict identity, composition, differential and augmentation clauses of the ring-family predicate verify the presheaf and chain-map equations. Apply module sheafification and its adjunction on complexes to the resulting augmentation.
